claims.text: Cocaine blocks Na channels: local anesthetic and dysrhythmogenic effects
claims.quote: Cocaine also blocks sodium channels, accounting for its local anesthetic and cardiac dysrhythmogenic properties.

claims.text: Case report: cocaine Na channel blockade worsens QRS widening; sodium bicarb can counteract it
claims.quote: Cocaine-induced sodium channel blockade exacerbates QRS widening, and sodium bicarbonate treatment can counteract this effect, potentially preventing a fatal outcome.
claims.locator: Not Your Typical V-Tach: Cocaine’s Cardiac Trickery (Spartan Med Res J, 2025)
